controls.requirement: Trust boundaries, entry points, sensitive assets, and external dependencies are identifiable from repository evidence.
Every privileged operation enforces function-, role-, object-, ownership-, and tenant-level authorization as applicable.
Identity proofing, authentication, session handling, recovery, and identity lifecycle controls are implemented when identities are in scope.
Untrusted input is validated at the trust boundary and interpreted only by parameterized or context-safe APIs.
Output is encoded, escaped, or serialized for its destination context.
File access, uploads, redirects, and outbound requests constrain paths, destinations, protocols, sizes, and content types.
Secrets are not committed and are retrieved, scoped, rotated, and redacted through an approved mechanism.
Approved cryptographic algorithms, randomness, key handling, and transport protections are used for sensitive data.
Production configuration uses secure defaults, least privilege, explicit exposure, and environment separation.
Dependencies are reproducibly pinned or locked and are checked against a current vulnerability advisory source.
Build inputs, generated artifacts, releases, and update channels have verifiable integrity and provenance.
Automation permissions, tokens, third-party actions, and deployment gates follow least privilege and immutable versioning.
Untrusted code, data, plugins, updates, and serialized objects are authenticated or constrained before use.
Exceptional conditions fail safely, preserve transaction integrity, release resources, and avoid sensitive disclosure.
Rate, size, concurrency, recursion, and time limits constrain attacker-controlled resource use.
Critical operations resist replay, races, duplicate execution, state manipulation, and abuse of workflow assumptions.
Security-relevant events are recorded with integrity and context without logging credentials or unnecessary sensitive data.
Material security events have actionable monitoring or alerting integration.
Sensitive data collection, storage, exposure, retention, backup, and deletion are minimized and controlled.
Tests cover negative cases, authorization boundaries, abuse cases, and regressions for security-sensitive behavior.
